title: Working with Psychiatry, being part of MDT's, History of Mental Health & Practically Managing Risk with Prof Graeme Yorston

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 各位心理学家，如果你们能赚到除了用时间换金钱以外的钱，那会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: Sophie Foote 的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于 2022 年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家完成他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得 Sophie 的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四场小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份 Fortnum and Mason 的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Beth, and I'm a psychological well-being practitioner from Newcastle.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫 Beth，是一名来自纽卡斯尔的心理健康从业者。

sentences.en: I just wanted to say the biggest thank you to the contributors of the Clinical Psychologist Collective book.
sentences.zh: 我只想对《临床心理学家集体》一书的贡献者们表示最诚挚的感谢。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed reading this so much and loved having an insight into the range of backgrounds and experiences people have prior to applying for the doctorate.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢读这本书，也很喜欢了解人们在申请博士学位之前的各种背景和经历。

sentences.en: And it's been really interesting seeing the potential barriers to the application as well and how I can try and work around this.
sentences.zh: 看到申请中潜在的障碍以及我如何尝试克服这些障碍，也非常有趣。

sentences.en: I really started to doubt myself and whether I was good enough to apply for the Clinical Psychology Doctorate.
sentences.zh: 我曾经非常怀疑自己，怀疑自己是否足够优秀去申请临床心理学博士学位。

sentences.en: But this has really given me the confidence boost that I needed to give it a shot.
sentences.zh: 但这本书确实给了我所需要的信心，让我决定试一试。

sentences.en: So, the biggest thank you ever.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次表示最衷心的感谢。

sentences.en: I welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到“有抱负的心理学家”播客。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening as ever, and thank you for all of your super kind comments.
sentences.zh: 一如既往地感谢大家的收听，也感谢大家所有超级友善的评论。

sentences.en: They're really gratefully received.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常感激。

sentences.en: I'd really love any audio testimonials for the podcast itself or any of the books, just so that I know that you're really enjoying what you're listening to.
sentences.zh: 我真的很希望能收到关于播客本身或任何书籍的音频感言，这样我就知道你们真的很喜欢听的内容。

sentences.en: And I'd really love to have any audio testimonials you might be willing to leave me for the podcast itself.
sentences.zh: 我非常希望能收到你们愿意为播客本身留下的任何音频感言。

sentences.en: For more information on how to do that, go to www.goodthinkingpsychology.co.uk forward slash podcast or the link will be there in the show notes for you too.
sentences.zh: 有关如何操作的更多信息，请访问 www.goodthinkingpsychology.co.uk/podcast，或者链接也会在节目说明中提供。

sentences.en: This is all about collaboration.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是关于合作。

sentences.en: And another great piece of collaboration is when we work as part of multidisciplinary teams, also called MDTs.
sentences.zh: 另一个伟大的合作形式是我们作为多学科团队（也称为 MDT）的一部分进行工作。

sentences.en: And being part of an MDT and having had MDT experience is something which is really useful for any aspiring psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 成为 MDT 的一员并拥有 MDT 经验，对于任何有抱负的心理学家来说都非常有益。

sentences.en: And it's something that often crops up, you know, for assistant psychologist interviews.
sentences.zh: 而且这在助理心理学家的面试中经常出现。

sentences.en: I learned my trade in working in multidisciplinary teams when I was at St. Andrew's Healthcare.
sentences.zh: 我在圣安德鲁斯医疗中心工作时学会了如何在多学科团队中工作。

sentences.en: That was the first MDT team that I had been part of.
sentences.zh: 那是我加入的第一个 MDT 团队。

sentences.en: And I was so fortunate that I'd been around such highly skilled and competent, caring, kind team members.
sentences.zh: 我非常幸运，身边有如此技术精湛、能干、关心他人且友善的团队成员。

sentences.en: And I learned a great deal from them.
sentences.zh: 我从他们身上学到了很多。

sentences.en: And they were, you know, kind and patient towards me as I developed my stripes as an aspiring psychologist too.
sentences.zh: 当我作为一名有抱负的心理学家逐渐成长时，他们对我非常友善和耐心。

sentences.en: So when I was thinking about reaching out to have a psychiatrist on the podcast, my first thoughts were of a psychiatrist that I had worked with as an aspiring psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我考虑邀请一位精神科医生参加播客时，我首先想到的是我作为有抱负的心理学家时曾共事过的一位精神科医生。

sentences.en: And so I was brave and I reached out and asked him if he would be willing to come along and record an episode for us.
sentences.zh: 于是我鼓起勇气联系了他，问他是否愿意来为我们录制一期节目。

sentences.en: And he was so kind and gracious and said that he would love to.
sentences.zh: 他非常友善和亲切，说他很乐意。

sentences.en: So I am thrilled to introduce you to someone I knew as a doctor.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴向大家介绍我曾以医生身份认识的一位朋友。

sentences.en: And since I have moved on to Pastor's New, he has gone on to become a professor.
sentences.zh: 自从我搬到 Pastor's New 之后，他已经成为了一名教授。

sentences.en: So you're going to be listening to me chatting with Professor Graham Yawston, who is a consultant psychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你现在听到的是我与精神科顾问医生 Graham Yawston 教授的谈话。

sentences.en: And today's episode is all about working with MDTs, but also about practical ways to manage risk as well,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目是关于与 MDT 合作，以及管理风险的实用方法，

sentences.en: which is something that psychiatrists are really good at and something that I learned a lot from my time working at St. Andrew's.
sentences.zh: 这是精神科医生非常擅长的领域，也是我在圣安德鲁斯工作期间学到很多的东西。

sentences.en: I hope you find this episode really useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这期节目非常有用。

sentences.en: And as ever, we welcome any comments, any questions.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我们欢迎任何评论和问题。

sentences.en: You can watch this on YouTube, but it is audio only.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 YouTube 上观看，但这只是音频。

sentences.en: So you'll just have lots of nice pictures to look at if you're watching on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在 YouTube 上观看，只会看到很多好看的图片。

sentences.en: If you're listening on Apple Podcast, please do rate and review.
sentences.zh: 如果你在 Apple Podcast 上收听，请务必评分和评论。

sentences.en: Be gratefully received.
sentences.zh: 我会非常感激。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I hope you find this episode useful.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，希望你觉得这期节目有用。

sentences.en: So welcome along.
sentences.zh: 那么，欢迎大家。

sentences.en: I just want to say hi and welcome our guest, Professor Graham Yawston.
sentences.zh: 我想打个招呼，欢迎我们的嘉宾 Graham Yawston 教授。

sentences.en: I'll let you introduce yourself.
sentences.zh: 请你做个自我介绍。

sentences.en: Hi, yes, I'm Graham Yawston.
sentences.zh: 嗨，是的，我是 Graham Yawston。

sentences.en: I am a forensic neuropsychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 我是一名法医神经精神科医生。

sentences.en: So I've had a wide range of experience in different areas of psychiatry, worked in different hospitals around the country,
sentences.zh: 我在精神病学的不同领域拥有广泛的经验，曾在全国各地的不同医院工作过，

sentences.en: in Scotland and England, and different levels of security.
sentences.zh: 在苏格兰和英格兰，以及不同安全级别的机构。

sentences.en: So from high secure, medium secure, low secure, and currently working in a rehab setting in Northampton.
sentences.zh: 从高安全、中安全、低安全级别，目前在北安普顿的一家康复机构工作。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: Our paths first crossed when I was an assistant psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们第一次交集是在我担任助理心理学家的时候。

sentences.en: So when I was looking at how to thicken the dialogue of psychiatry and psychology, you were the first person I thought of.
sentences.zh: 所以当我思考如何加深精神病学和心理学之间的对话时，你是我第一个想到的人。

sentences.en: But I am a little bit daunted to have you here.
sentences.zh: 但我在这里感到有点畏惧。

sentences.en: I can't imagine why you'd be daunted.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象你为什么会感到畏惧。

sentences.en: No, I think, you know, assistant psychologists do perform a really important part of MDTs.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为，你知道，助理心理学家在 MDT 中确实发挥着非常重要的作用。

sentences.en: And I think it is difficult because, you know, particularly if you're a brand new assistant psychologist,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这很困难，因为，你知道，特别是如果你是一个全新的助理心理学家，

sentences.en: you're quite young and everybody else in the team is usually a bit older and they may have years and years of experience.
sentences.zh: 你还很年轻，而团队中的其他人通常年纪稍大，他们可能拥有多年的经验。

sentences.en: But there's absolutely nothing to be daunted by most people in MDTs are very nice and very welcoming.
sentences.zh: 但绝对没有什么好畏惧的，MDT 中的大多数人都非常友善和热情。

sentences.en: They certainly are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此。

sentences.en: And I always felt very welcome in the teams when I worked with you.
sentences.zh: 当我与你共事时，我总是感到在团队中非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你。

sentences.en: I do remember you didn't really like my hair accessories at the time and you had a very valid point.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得你当时不太喜欢我的发饰，而且你说的很有道理。

sentences.en: I only remember I had some sort of crazy chopsticks in my hair and you were like, someone could easily poke you in the eye with those.
sentences.zh: 我只记得我头发上插着一些奇怪的筷子，你说有人很容易用那些东西戳到我的眼睛。

sentences.en: I was like, hmm, yes, you may be right.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，是的，你可能是对的。

sentences.en: Gosh, I think the Alzheimer's must be catching up with me.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我想一定是阿尔茨海默症找上我了。

sentences.en: I don't actually remember that.
sentences.zh: 我其实不记得那件事了。

sentences.en: No, you mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 不，你提到了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's the kind of important issue of kind of risk awareness that somebody right at the start of their career
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是一个关于风险意识的重要问题，职业生涯刚开始的人

sentences.en: just may not think about things like that that could be used as a potential weapon in a secure unit where people have a history of serious violence.
sentences.zh: 可能根本不会想到那些东西在有严重暴力史的安全单位里可能被用作潜在武器。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I did give it back to you, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实反驳了你。

sentences.en: I did say, well, they could whip the pen out of your pocket as well, Dr. Euston.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，他们也可以从你的口袋里掏出钢笔，Euston 医生。

sentences.en: And you were like, yeah, but then I'd know they'd done that.
sentences.zh: 你说，是的，但那样我就知道他们做了。

sentences.en: You wouldn't know if they were behind you.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在你身后，你就不会知道了。

sentences.en: And I was like, all right, you're totally right.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: I never wore them again to work, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我再也没有戴过它们去上班。

sentences.en: Very sensible.
sentences.zh: 非常明智。

sentences.en: I did take a pen in and you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我确实带了一支笔进去，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: So pens are a potential weapon.
sentences.zh: 所以笔也是潜在的武器。

sentences.en: And in some of the most acute wards in high-secure hospitals, you have to leave your pens in store
sentences.zh: 在一些高安全医院最急性的病房里，你必须把笔留在储藏室，

sentences.en: and you are only allowed to use those little tiny stubby pens that, you know, that kind of three or four inches long.
sentences.zh: 而且只允许使用那种三四英寸长的小短笔。

sentences.en: Like you steal from Asda.
sentences.zh: 就像你从 Asda 偷来的那种。

sentences.en: Not Asda, Argos.
sentences.zh: 不是 Asda，是 Argos。

sentences.en: That's the ones.
sentences.zh: 就是那种。

sentences.en: We don't condone stealing here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不纵容偷窃。

sentences.en: No, definitely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: They've switched them to pencils now, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们现在把笔换成铅笔了，你知道吗。

sentences.en: You can still hurt someone seriously with a pencil.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以用铅笔严重伤害别人。

sentences.en: And, you know, particularly if it's a really sharp pencil, you can do a lot of damage.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，特别是如果是一支非常尖的铅笔，你可以造成很大的伤害。

sentences.en: And certainly in one of the hospitals that I worked at, it was damage to people's eyes that were the kind of preferred,
sentences.zh: 当然，在我工作过的一家医院里，人们眼睛受到的伤害是那种首选的，

sentences.en: I didn't sound quite the right word, but it was a not uncommon form of attack was to, yeah, stab people in the eye with a pen or a pencil.
sentences.zh: “首选”这个词可能不太准确，但那是一种并不罕见的攻击方式，就是用钢笔或铅笔戳人的眼睛。

sentences.en: So you're absolutely right to highlight the risk of me wearing chopsticks to work.
sentences.zh: 所以你强调我戴筷子上班的风险是完全正确的。

sentences.en: So thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你。

sentences.en: But it's an important area to consider, isn't it, when we're working with risk, especially not even when we're working in forensic services.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个需要考虑的重要领域，不是吗？当我们处理风险时，即使不是在法医服务部门工作。

sentences.en: You know, any setting we're working in, even someone we think we know really well, could potentially be risky.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在任何环境下工作，即使是我们认为非常了解的人，也可能存在风险。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think this is a really important point to get across.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个非常重要的观点。

sentences.en: If you're working in a high-secure hospital, then you're going to get a lot of induction about risk
sentences.zh: 如果你在高安全医院工作，那么你会接受很多关于风险的入职培训，

sentences.en: and you're going to be well aware that you're dealing with people who could pose a risk to you.
sentences.zh: 并且你会清楚地意识到你正在处理的人可能会对你构成风险。

sentences.en: But if you're working in an outpatient setting or an acute psychiatry inpatient setting, then that's the first point of contact that people will have with mental health services.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在门诊或急性精神科住院部工作，那是人们接触心理健康服务的第一个接触点。

sentences.en: So some of those people who do eventually end up in high-secure hospital have started in those services.
sentences.zh: 所以一些最终进入高安全医院的人是从这些服务开始的。

sentences.en: So they might have all those kind of aggressive tendencies.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能拥有所有那些攻击倾向。

sentences.en: They just haven't been, no one knows about them yet.
sentences.zh: 只是还没有人知道他们而已。

sentences.en: So you have to at least be aware of the potential for aggression and make sure that you're safe,
sentences.zh: 所以你至少要意识到攻击的可能性，并确保你是安全的，

sentences.en: make sure that you can get out of an interview room and not put yourself at risk in any way.
sentences.zh: 确保你能从面试室出来，并且不会以任何方式让自己处于危险之中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I still remember setting up the room quite carefully.
sentences.zh: 我仍然记得当时非常小心地布置房间。

sentences.en: I vividly remember you dragging chairs around to make sure that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得你拖动椅子，以确保，你知道，

sentences.en: you were going to be able to get out of rooms and the staff were if we needed to and that there were enough escorts
sentences.zh: 如果你需要的话，你能够从房间里出来，工作人员也能出来，而且有足够的护送人员，

sentences.en: or people trained in restraint when we were all trained in restraint, weren't we?
sentences.zh: 或者受过约束训练的人，我们当时都受过约束训练，不是吗？

sentences.en: But to be able to, you know, have the best possible outcome from any situation.
sentences.zh: 但为了能够，你知道，从任何情况中获得最好的结果。

sentences.en: It's about thinking in advance, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是关于提前思考，不是吗？

sentences.en: And planning for the worst, preparing for the worst and hoping it won't happen.
sentences.zh: 为最坏的情况做计划，为最坏的情况做准备，并希望它不会发生。

sentences.en: Definitely, yes.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: And I think, so, you know, you've got to stay in control if you are in a hospital or any kind of healthcare setting of getting the room positioned before the person comes in.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，如果你在医院或任何医疗机构，你必须保持控制，在人进来之前把房间布置好。

sentences.en: Always looks a bit strange if you're moving furniture around once they're in.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在里面时你还在移动家具，看起来总是有点奇怪。

sentences.en: But, you know, get yourself so that you are closest to the door.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，让自己离门最近。

sentences.en: And I have done that time and time again all throughout my career.
sentences.zh: 在我的整个职业生涯中，我一次又一次地这样做。

sentences.en: Even in children's services, I was always closest to the door because I've learned from you and from our late colleague, Dr. Wood, how to, you know,
sentences.zh: 即使在儿童服务部门，我也总是离门最近，因为我从你和我们已故的同事 Wood 医生那里学到了如何，你知道，

sentences.en: how to ensure that your safety and the patient's safety is optimised.
sentences.zh: 如何确保你和病人的安全得到优化。

sentences.en: Yeah, these are very important lessons.
sentences.zh: 是的，这些是非常重要的教训。

sentences.en: I'm glad that, I'm surprised that I was the first person to tell you about that.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴，我很惊讶我是第一个告诉你这件事的人。

sentences.en: But it is, those are important lessons that, you know, get into a good habit early in your career and always stick with it.
sentences.zh: 但确实，这些都是重要的教训，你知道，在职业生涯早期养成良好的习惯，并始终坚持下去。

sentences.en: It'll just become second nature, then you won't think about it.
sentences.zh: 这会成为第二天性，然后你就不会再考虑它了。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And one of my top tips that I learned was pop your diary on your chair when you go and get the patient so they can't sit in your chair.
sentences.zh: 我学到的顶级技巧之一是，当你去接病人时，把你的日记本放在你的椅子上，这样他们就不能坐在你的椅子上了。

sentences.en: And it's quite interesting when they try to or they give you your diary back and then you have to say, actually, I'm going to sit there.
sentences.zh: 当他们尝试这样做，或者他们把日记本还给你，然后你不得不说，其实我要坐那里，这很有趣。

sentences.en: It's a test of kind of social norms as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是对社会规范的一种考验。

sentences.en: That sounds interesting.
sentences.zh: 听起来很有趣。

sentences.en: I don't think you learned that one from me because that's a really good tip, actually.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你是从我这里学到的，因为那确实是一个非常好的技巧。

sentences.en: I have to remember that one myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也得记住那个。

sentences.en: I have useful strategies as well.
sentences.zh: 我也有有用的策略。

sentences.en: You also taught me something that you may not know that you taught me, but I use every day.
sentences.zh: 你还教了我一些你可能不知道你教过我的东西，但我每天都在用。

sentences.en: So I often used to do the notes in our ward round sessions.
sentences.zh: 我过去经常在我们的查房会议上做笔记。

sentences.en: But sometimes you would do it and you were doing something on the computer.
sentences.zh: 但有时你会做，你在电脑上做一些事情。

sentences.en: And I thought, how did he do that?
sentences.zh: 我想，他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: And you introduced me to using the delete button to delete text that you've already typed, just to hold your finger on it.
sentences.zh: 你教我使用删除键来删除已经输入的文本，只需按住它即可。

sentences.en: Whereas before I met you, I was backspacing every single thing.
sentences.zh: 而在遇到你之前，我是在逐个退格删除所有内容。

sentences.en: So every time I do that, I do think of you.
sentences.zh: 所以每次我这样做，我都会想到你。

sentences.en: Heavens, me teaching someone that IT, that sounds highly improbable, but I'll take your word for it.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我教别人 IT，这听起来极不可能，但我相信你说的。

sentences.en: You'll have to tell your children and they'll be delighted.
sentences.zh: 你得告诉你孩子们，他们会很高兴的。

sentences.en: Back in the day, I was a relatively new adopter of information technology, but I feel like a dinosaur nowadays because it's all moving way too fast for me.
sentences.zh: 过去，我是信息技术的相对较新的采用者，但现在我觉得自己像个恐龙，因为一切对我来说发展得太快了。

sentences.en: Well, you were an influencer when it came to me and the delete key.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我和删除键的关系上，你确实起到了推波助澜的作用。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你。

sentences.en: Have you learned anything along your career from a random source that's been really useful or something that you can think of that you think,
sentences.zh: 在你的职业生涯中，有没有从某个意想不到的来源学到过什么真正有用的东西，或者有什么让你觉得，

sentences.en: oh, well, that was really important for me or I use that all the time?
sentences.zh: 哦，那对我来说真的很重要，或者我一直在用它？

sentences.en: And you wouldn't necessarily have known that you were planning to learn it at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且你当时未必知道自己正打算去学它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think, you know, training as a doctor is very much an apprenticeship.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，你知道，医生培训在很大程度上是一种学徒制。

sentences.en: So, you know, obviously a lot of your facts, your knowledge comes from books and papers and things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，显然你的很多事实和知识都来自书籍、论文之类的东西。

sentences.en: But actually how to deal with people, how to approach people, how to interact with team members is very much about seeing, you know, being in teams,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如何与人打交道，如何接近他人，如何与团队成员互动，很大程度上在于观察，你知道，身处团队之中，

sentences.en: observing how those teams interact and then going, yeah, I like the way this person is running his or her team.
sentences.zh: 观察这些团队是如何互动的，然后心想，嗯，我喜欢这个人管理他或她团队的方式。

sentences.en: And that's how I would want to be.
sentences.zh: 那就是我想要成为的样子。

sentences.en: And equally, seeing people doing it not so well and being a little bit too formal or whatever it might be, I'm thinking, yeah, that doesn't, I don't want to do it that way.
sentences.zh: 同样地，看到别人做得不那么好，或者表现得太正式之类的，我就会想，嗯，我不希望那样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And how to position yourself in teams can be so important, can't it?
sentences.zh: 而且在团队中如何定位自己非常重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I think this is one of the key issues for assistant psychologists because you're coming into a team.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是助理心理学家面临的关键问题之一，因为你是新加入一个团队。

sentences.en: You probably don't know people very well.
sentences.zh: 你可能不太了解大家。

sentences.en: The team may be very established and have been, you know, going along for years of good relationships.
sentences.zh: 这个团队可能已经非常成熟，并且，你知道，多年来一直保持着良好的关系。

sentences.en: There might be people with years and years of clinical experience.
sentences.zh: 可能还有拥有多年临床经验的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, on your first day, you go into this ward round and see the sea of faces that you don't know.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，第一天上班，你走进查房现场，看到一群你不认识的面孔。

sentences.en: How do you fit into that team?
sentences.zh: 你该如何融入那个团队？

sentences.en: And what do you do?
sentences.zh: 你该怎么做？

sentences.en: Do you be a big personality and kind of, you know, introduce yourself at full volume?
sentences.zh: 是表现得个性十足，然后，你知道，大声地自我介绍吗？

sentences.en: Or do you kind of just sit in the back row and be very meek and mild and hardly say a thing?
sentences.zh: 还是坐在后排，表现得非常温顺、文静，几乎一言不发？

sentences.en: And it's very difficult, I think, to break into that team and to be aware that that's, you know, that requires effort and work and thinking about, I think, is important.
sentences.zh: 我认为，想要打入那个团队是非常困难的，而且要意识到这需要付出努力、思考和投入，我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: I think the more that you make a conscious effort to think about, well, how am I going to do this, you know, the better it's likely to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为你越是有意识地去思考，嗯，我该怎么做，你知道，情况就越可能会好转。

sentences.en: And every team is going to be different.
sentences.zh: 而且每个团队都是不同的。

sentences.en: So, as I say, you know, I've worked in a huge number of different environments.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我所说，你知道，我在很多不同的环境中工作过。

sentences.en: And the extent to which the medical model is dominant varies between teaMs.
sentences.zh: 医疗模式在不同团队中占据主导地位的程度各不相同。

sentences.en: And therefore, the extent to which psychological input into those teams is going to be absolutely integral or slightly peripheral is going to is also going to vary.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学投入在这些团队中是绝对不可或缺的，还是稍微处于边缘地位，也会有所不同。

sentences.en: And I would say, you know, as a new AP, joining a team, listen, observe relatively quietly.
sentences.zh: 所以我会说，你知道，作为一名新入职的助理心理学家，加入一个团队时，要听，要安静地观察。

sentences.en: You don't want to be completely anonymous.
sentences.zh: 你不想完全默默无闻。

sentences.en: But, you know, don't go in with a big personality and big opinions straight off because people are just going to look at you and think, hmm, who is this person?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，不要一上来就表现得个性张扬、观点鲜明，因为人们只会看着你，心想，嗯，这个人是谁？

sentences.en: So, you know, observe, be helpful to the team.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，观察，对团队有所帮助。

sentences.en: So, one of the things I've always done is occasionally make coffee so that absolutely everybody in the team is, you know, is part of that rotor.
sentences.zh: 所以，我一直做的一件事就是偶尔煮煮咖啡，这样团队里的每个人，你知道，都在轮值名单里。

sentences.en: No one is above going and making coffee for everybody else.
sentences.zh: 没有人高高在上到不用去为其他人煮咖啡。

sentences.en: And that helps bonding.
sentences.zh: 这有助于建立感情。

sentences.en: So, again, depending on how the kind of MDT meetings are organised, usually patients will be brought into those meetings.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，取决于多学科团队（MDT）会议的组织方式，通常患者会被带到这些会议中。

sentences.en: And I think it works really well if right from the beginning, as an assistant psychologist, you say, oh, you know, would you like me to go and get the patient?
sentences.zh: 我认为如果从一开始，作为一名助理心理学家，你说，哦，你知道，需要我去接患者吗？这样效果会很好。

sentences.en: Rather than relying on one person to do that.
sentences.zh: 而不是依赖某一个人去做这件事。

sentences.en: And also, I think, understanding what the model of the psychology input to the team is.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为，理解心理学对团队的投入模式也很重要。

sentences.en: Is it a totally integrated approach?
sentences.zh: 这是一种完全整合的方法吗？

sentences.en: Are you there every week for every MDT meeting or ward round?
sentences.zh: 你每周都会参加所有的MDT会议或查房吗？

sentences.en: Every CPA, are you there on that ward and it's your ward?
sentences.zh: 所有的护理计划评估（CPA），你都在那个病房，那是你的病房吗？

sentences.en: Or is it more of a kind of referral model?
sentences.zh: 还是更像是一种转诊模式？

sentences.en: And if it's a referral model and you're just going to occasional ones, then that's fine to then ask for referrals.
sentences.zh: 如果这是转诊模式，你只是偶尔参加几次，那么要求转诊是可以的。

sentences.en: But if you're in part of an integrated team, then there's nothing worse than if somebody in the team is saying it would be really helpful to have a psychology opinion on this.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是整合团队的一部分，那么最糟糕的事情莫过于团队里有人说，如果能有心理学方面的意见会很有帮助。

sentences.en: To then say, all right, great, thank you.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，好的，太棒了，谢谢。

sentences.en: Can you do a referral, please?
sentences.zh: 你能做一个转诊吗，请？

sentences.en: It is probably the thing that gets me, not irritated, it's not as strong as that, but just frustrated more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 这大概是让我，不是说被激怒，还没到那种程度，但比起其他任何事情，这更让我感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's tricky.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这很棘手。

sentences.en: Certainly in community services where I've worked, you kind of can't launch in straight away.
sentences.zh: 当然，在我工作过的社区服务中，你不能一上来就大干一场。

sentences.en: But when you're on an inpatient ward and you're all there anyway, you know, it feels like you can come to the fore a little bit more quickly, you know, and, yeah,
sentences.zh: 但当你在住院病房，反正大家都在那里，你知道，感觉你可以更快地走到前台，你知道，而且，是的，

sentences.en: support on the ground without additional forMs.
sentences.zh: 在没有额外表格的情况下提供实地支持。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, so being aware of, I mean, everybody is time pressured.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，意识到这一点，我的意思是，每个人都有时间压力。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that any one professional group is less time pressured than any other, but particularly for nurses and doctors, you're constantly reprioritizing.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说任何一个专业群体比其他群体承受的时间压力小，但特别是对于护士和医生来说，你一直在重新确定优先级。

sentences.en: And that is something that happens less, I think, in psychology.
sentences.zh: 而我认为，这种情况在心理学领域发生得较少。

sentences.en: You're often able, you have a luxury of being able to kind of work through a kind of a to-do list without constantly having to put things on.
sentences.zh: 你通常能够，你有幸能够处理一份待办事项清单，而不必不断地把事情放上去。

sentences.en: I've got to move this one forward and that one back.
sentences.zh: 我得把这个往前推，把那个往后推。

sentences.en: At least that's my impression.
sentences.zh: 至少这是我的印象。

sentences.en: Tell me if I'm completely wrong on that, but that's my impression.
sentences.zh: 如果我完全错了，请告诉我，但这就是我的印象。

sentences.en: And so the kind of the urgency of things sometimes feels more than people from nursing and medical backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时事情的紧迫感感觉比护理和医学背景的人要强。

sentences.en: And just being aware of that really, I think, is important.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，意识到这一点真的很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think even since when I was working alongside you, the expectations on unqualified psychologists has gone through the roof.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为即使从我和你一起工作时算起，对非合格心理学家的期望也已经高得离谱了。

sentences.en: So I didn't hold my own caseload when I was working with you.
sentences.zh: 所以我跟你工作时并没有负责自己的病例。

sentences.en: I was very much to support the psychologist and the psychology functions, but also the MDT.
sentences.zh: 我主要是支持心理学家和心理学职能，但也支持MDT。

sentences.en: So, you know, I might have done the odd bit of neuropsych here and there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我可能偶尔做一点神经心理学方面的工作。

sentences.en: I was doing, you know, the monitoring and the recording of all of the sexually inappropriate behaviors and the, you know,
sentences.zh: 我在做，你知道，监测和记录所有性不当行为，以及，你知道，

sentences.en: the aggression and reporting on those for the ward rounds and things.
sentences.zh: 攻击行为，并为查房等事情进行报告。

sentences.en: But I didn't hold my own caseload,
sentences.zh: 但我没有负责自己的病例，

sentences.en: whereas actually what's happened in the time since I was an aspiring psychologist is that people are being encouraged to hold their own caseloads as well.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，自从我作为一名有抱负的心理学家以来，人们也被鼓励去负责自己的病例了。

sentences.en: And people are working, you know, sometimes even as much as, you know, 80, 90 percent of their whole time equivalent hours are face-to-face client times.
sentences.zh: 而且人们工作，你知道，有时甚至高达，你知道，80%到90%的全职等效工时都是面对面的客户时间。

sentences.en: And that is that's a big pressure.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的压力。

sentences.en: It's a big change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: And the level of even the level of risk and responsibility that aspiring psychologists are being asked to hold these times, you know, these times.
sentences.zh: 甚至是有抱负的心理学家在这些时候被要求承担的风险和责任水平，你知道，这些时候。

sentences.en: I grew into that responsibility and we're asking a lot more a lot sooner, I think, which gives you less room for a little bit of playfulness and less room to, you know,
sentences.zh: 我是在那种责任中成长起来的，而我认为我们要求得更多、更快，这让你减少了一点点玩耍的空间，也减少了，你知道，

sentences.en: to make those mistakes and to learn by watching other people do it.
sentences.zh: 犯错和通过观察别人做事来学习的空间。

sentences.en: Because there's more pressure on you.
sentences.zh: 因为你身上的压力更大了。

sentences.en: You know, like you said, it's nice to come in and grow into a role.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像你说的，进入一个角色并慢慢成长起来是很好的。

sentences.en: But actually, a lot of aspiring psychologists are finding that they're kind of being, you know,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，许多有抱负的心理学家发现他们正被，你知道，

sentences.en: farmed out and put on the production line and expected to perform almost from day one.
sentences.zh: 外包出去，放在生产线上，几乎从第一天起就被要求表现出色。

sentences.en: And it's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这非常困难。

sentences.en: OK, that really does sound like being thrown in at the deep end.
sentences.zh: 好的，那听起来确实像是被扔进了深水区。

sentences.en: And my sense is that that is how I learned as a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，我作为一名医生就是这样学习的。

sentences.en: And I think most other people, you know, learn that the old kind of maxim of see one, do one, teach one.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为大多数其他人，你知道，学习的是那种古老的格言：看一个，做一个，教一个。

sentences.en: You know, you see some procedure once you then expected to be able to do it yourself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你观察某个程序一次，然后就被期望能够自己做出来。

sentences.en: And then once you've done one, you're expected to teach everybody else how to do it.
sentences.zh: 一旦你做过一次，你就被期望教别人怎么做。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's right, but it you certainly your your pace of learning is is much more than if you if you start off very cautiously and spend a lot of time observing.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是对的，但你的学习速度肯定比你一开始非常谨慎并花大量时间观察要快得多。

sentences.en: You're going to learn an awful lot more from doing than you are from watching someone else do.
sentences.zh: 比起看别人做，你从自己动手中学到的东西要多得多。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's interesting that you're saying that I perhaps hadn't hadn't realized that there'd been that change.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你说得很有趣，我可能没有意识到已经发生了那种变化。

sentences.en: So it's tough, but it will definitely, you know, help people decide more quickly if they're in the right career and if it suits them.
sentences.zh: 所以这很艰难，但这肯定会，你知道，帮助人们更快地决定他们是否选择了正确的职业，以及它是否适合他们。

sentences.en: And there is that, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且确实有那种情况，不是吗？

sentences.en: There is burnout in our profession as a mental health professional, especially during the pandemic, you know,
sentences.zh: 作为一名心理健康专业人员，我们的职业中存在职业倦怠，特别是在疫情期间，你知道，

sentences.en: because there wasn't any working from home when there's patients to go in and support who are living in inpatient units.
sentences.zh: 因为当有患者需要去住院部支持时，根本没有居家办公这回事。

sentences.en: It's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这非常困难。

sentences.en: How's your experience of burnout been in the profession and how to support and nurture members of the team to try to reduce burnout?
sentences.zh: 你在职业生涯中对职业倦怠的体验如何，以及如何支持和培养团队成员以尝试减少职业倦怠？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it is very important and it has been very, very tough.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这非常重要，而且一直非常、非常艰难。

sentences.en: I mean, my my current job, as I say, is a rehab unit and we're trying to all the time help people become reintegrated into the community.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我所说，我目前的工作是在一个康复中心，我们一直在努力帮助人们重新融入社区。

sentences.en: And to then try and do that when they were literally were not allowed outside the hospital,
sentences.zh: 当他们实际上不被允许离开医院时，还要尝试这样做，

sentences.en: the kind of the national guidelines and then the local public health guidelines that said, actually, you're a hospital, therefore, your patients aren't allowed out.
sentences.zh: 那种国家指导方针，然后是当地公共卫生指导方针说，实际上，你们是医院，因此，你们的患者不允许外出。

sentences.en: And that was for months on end.
sentences.zh: 那是持续了几个月的时间。

sentences.en: And it was very tough for the patients.
sentences.zh: 这对患者来说非常艰难。

sentences.en: Absolutely, amazingly well in coping with that.
sentences.zh: 绝对令人惊叹地应对得很好。

sentences.en: But it was also tough on staff because it meant that they were having to be constantly thinking of new things to do to stop people getting bored
sentences.zh: 但这对员工来说也很艰难，因为这意味着他们必须不断地想出新的事情来做，以防止人们感到无聊，

sentences.en: and to try and recreate some of the things that they will be doing if they were in the community.
sentences.zh: 并试图重现一些如果他们在社区里就会做的事情。

sentences.en: So we had about a million and one barbecues and things and, you know, just just try to to keep fresh was a real challenge.
sentences.zh: 所以我们举办了大约一百万零一次烧烤之类的活动，你知道，只是试图保持新鲜感真的是一个挑战。

sentences.en: But I think burnout generally is is an important issue.
sentences.zh: 但我认为职业倦怠通常是一个重要的问题。

sentences.en: It's people do talk about it, but often slightly reluctant to talk about their own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 人们确实会谈论它，但往往有点不愿谈论自己的问题。

sentences.en: I've certainly had problems in my own career, times where things got very difficult and you need to be able to talk to someone if if you feel things building up,
sentences.zh: 我的职业生涯中肯定也遇到过问题，有时情况变得非常困难，如果你感到事情在堆积，如果你不喜欢你的工作，如果你，你知道，你早上醒来只是想，哦，天哪，我不能，

sentences.en: if you're not enjoying your work, if you, you know, you kind of wake up in the morning and just think, oh, God, I can't.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要能够找人倾诉，

sentences.en: I don't want to go in.
sentences.zh: 我不想去上班。

sentences.en: I can't face it.
sentences.zh: 我无法面对它。

sentences.en: Then that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 那这就是个问题。

sentences.en: And you need to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 你需要谈谈这件事。

sentences.en: And there's usually resolutions to these things.
sentences.zh: 而且这些事情通常有解决办法。

sentences.en: And it may be that, you know, a change of scene, a change of team.
sentences.zh: 可能，你知道，换个环境，换个团队。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we're both lucky that we've worked with with great teams and great team members.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我们都很幸运，我们曾与很棒的团队和很棒的团队成员一起工作。

sentences.en: But sometimes teams don't function very well.
sentences.zh: 但有时团队运作得并不好。

sentences.en: And if you're in one of these.
sentences.zh: 如果你身处其中之一。

sentences.en: Well, let's call a toxic team.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们称之为有毒的团队。

sentences.en: They do exiSt. It's it's horrible.
sentences.zh: 它们确实存在。这很可怕。

sentences.en: And sometimes the only thing you can do is get out of that as quickly as possible or at least limit your kind of exposure to the toxicity.
sentences.zh: 有时你能做的唯一事情就是尽快离开，或者至少限制你接触这种毒性的程度。

sentences.en: So absolutely talking to your supervisor and being kind of open and honest about things.
sentences.zh: 所以绝对要和你的主管谈谈，对事情保持开放和诚实。

sentences.en: Honesty is always the best policy.
sentences.zh: 诚实永远是最好的政策。

sentences.en: You know, people worry if I kind of worry or sound like I'm moaning, then I might not get a good reference.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们担心如果我担心或者听起来像是在抱怨，那么我可能得不到好的推荐信。

sentences.en: But it's far better to be honest, I think, and deal with probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但我认为诚实并处理问题要好得多。

sentences.en: You know, you can get you can get bullying.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可能会遇到欺凌。

sentences.en: You can get inappropriate attention.
sentences.zh: 你可能会遇到不恰当的关注。

sentences.en: All sorts of issues can arise.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的问题都可能出现。

sentences.en: And you have to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 你必须处理它。

sentences.en: I think you have to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须处理它。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love that idea, actually, about thinking about maybe it's not me.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的很喜欢那个想法，关于考虑也许不是我的问题。

sentences.en: You know, maybe I'm OK.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许我没问题。

sentences.en: Maybe the problem is the environment here.
sentences.zh: 也许问题在于这里的环境。

sentences.en: Maybe this is a toxic team.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一个有毒的团队。

sentences.en: And people often say to me, well, I'm a bit worried about just having like a six month post or a four month post on my CV and how that looks.
sentences.zh: 人们经常对我说，嗯，我有点担心我的简历上只有六个月或四个月的职位，看起来会怎么样。

sentences.en: And it's like, actually, you know, you're the golden goose.
sentences.zh: 就像是，实际上，你知道，你是金鹅。

sentences.en: You have to look after you.
sentences.zh: 你必须照顾好你自己。

sentences.en: And if this isn't a good fit for you, it's OK to say no.
sentences.zh: 如果这不适合你，说不也是可以的。

sentences.en: It's OK to say, actually, I'm going elsewhere because this is not OK for me.
sentences.zh: 说，实际上，我要去别的地方，因为这对我来说不合适，是可以的。

sentences.en: This is not how I, you know, like your values of how to treat people.
sentences.zh: 这不是我，你知道，喜欢你对待人的价值观。

sentences.en: This is not how I think it's OK to treat people.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这样对待人是可以的。

sentences.en: And I'm going to vote with my feet.
sentences.zh: 我要用我的行动来投票。

sentences.en: You know, I'm going to use my voice.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我要发出我的声音。

sentences.en: And if saying no is not making a difference, you can be empowered and you can make different choices to go elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 如果说不没有带来改变，你可以获得授权，你可以做出不同的选择去别的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And it is tricky.
sentences.zh: 而且这很棘手。

sentences.en: I think it's maybe, well, in some ways,
sentences.zh: 我想也许，嗯，在某些方面，

sentences.en: it's slightly easier towards the end of your career or once you've had a few years under your belt because you've got some experience to draw on.
sentences.zh: 在职业生涯后期，或者当你工作了几年之后，情况会稍微容易一些，因为你已经积累了一些可以借鉴的经验。

sentences.en: At the start of your career, it's very hard to say, actually, this just is not working for me.
sentences.zh: 在职业生涯刚开始时，要说“这真的不适合我”，其实是非常困难的。

sentences.en: But, you know, trust yourself and, you know, follow your instincts is what I would say.
sentences.zh: 但我会说，要相信自己，追随你的直觉。

sentences.en: And if it just feels horrible when you go to work, that is not normal.
sentences.zh: 如果你去上班时感觉非常糟糕，那是不正常的。

sentences.en: It's not right.
sentences.zh: 这不对劲。

sentences.en: And you shouldn't put up with it.
sentences.zh: 你不应该忍受这种情况。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I'll have to say working with you was not a toxic environment.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，和你一起工作并不是一种有毒的环境。

sentences.en: I really, really enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我真的、真的很享受那段时光。

sentences.en: Leaving, leaving St. Andrews was really difficult for me from a really supportive, really cohesive,
sentences.zh: 离开圣安德鲁斯（St. Andrews）对我来说真的很困难，因为那里有一个非常支持、非常团结、

sentences.en: really big and broad team to then going somewhere very much smaller in the NHS where I was the only assistant.
sentences.zh: 规模很大且包容的团队，然后我去了国民医疗服务体系（NHS）一个非常小的地方，我是那里唯一的助理。

sentences.en: There was one qualified forensic psychologiSt. It couldn't have been, you know, a tiny little health care building couldn't have been more different.
sentences.zh: 当时只有一位合格的法医心理学家。那真是一个小小的医疗机构，再没有比这更不同的了。

sentences.en: And I really mourned for all of you when I left.
sentences.zh: 我离开时真的为你们所有人感到难过。

sentences.en: You know, it's still it's important to build different portfolios of your work across the across your career.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在你的职业生涯中建立不同的工作组合仍然是很重要的。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it's really hard to replicate what you guys are offering in terms of experience and nurturance as well.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，在经验和培养方面，真的很难复制你们所提供的那些东西。

sentences.en: And really good staff parties.
sentences.zh: 还有非常棒的员工聚会。

sentences.en: I'm glad you enjoyed those.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你喜欢那些聚会。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, St. Andrews, I would say at the time you were there, most of the time that I was there was a fantastic place to work.
sentences.zh: 是的，圣安德鲁斯，我想说在你待在那里的时候，以及我在那里的绝大部分时间里，那都是一个非常棒的工作场所。

sentences.en: And I know that it, you know, it helped many kind of psychologists go on to bigger and better things.
sentences.zh: 我知道它帮助了许多心理学家去追求更大、更好的成就。

sentences.en: It was a great place to do research and and just make those kind of take those first footsteps towards, you know, just, you know,
sentences.zh: 那是一个进行研究的好地方，也是迈出第一步的好地方，你知道，

sentences.en: having a bit more on your CV than just clinical work.
sentences.zh: 让你的简历上不仅仅只有临床工作经验。

sentences.en: Getting involved in research is is so important.
sentences.zh: 参与研究非常重要。

sentences.en: And my current post at St. Matthew's Health Care,
sentences.zh: 我在圣马修斯医疗保健中心（St. Matthew's Health Care）目前的职位，

sentences.en: that's one of the things that I've been trying to do is get and encourage assistant psychologists to to be involved in very simple little research projects.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力做的一件事就是鼓励助理心理学家参与一些非常简单的小型研究项目。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't have to be some massive international collaboration study, just, you know, case report, getting that done as a poster or kind of writing up an audit,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它不必是什么大型的国际合作研究，只要是病例报告、做成海报，或者写一份审计报告之类的，

sentences.en: all those kind of things just gives you a bit more on your CV.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都能让你的简历更丰富一些。

sentences.en: It also helps helps build relationships.
sentences.zh: 它也有助于建立人际关系。

sentences.en: And however, I'm a great believer in research and and and the the advantages really that research brings to helping you think about about anything, really.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我非常相信研究，也相信研究在帮助你思考任何事情方面所带来的优势。

sentences.en: Obviously, if you're writing a paper, it will be about that particular topic, but it's how you approach any topic in in your career is important, I think.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你在写论文，它会是关于那个特定的主题，但我认为，你如何处理职业生涯中的任何主题才是重要的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And, you know, research is so important.
sentences.zh: 而且，研究非常重要。

sentences.en: It's one of the key aspects for aspiring psychologists.
sentences.zh: 这是有抱负的心理学家的关键方面之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, you get separate points on your forms for research.
sentences.zh: 而且，你在申请表上会因为研究而获得额外的分数。

sentences.en: So I did my first piece of published research was at St. Andrews.
sentences.zh: 我发表的第一篇研究就是在圣安德鲁斯完成的。

sentences.en: And if Dr. Yorston, as you were at the time, you know, professor, had asked me to get involved, I'd have snapped your hand off.
sentences.zh: 如果当时的约斯顿（Yorston）博士，也就是现在的教授，让我参与的话，我肯定会毫不犹豫地答应。

sentences.en: I can't believe I didn't ask you.
sentences.zh: 真不敢相信我当时没问你。

sentences.en: I'm always asking.
sentences.zh: 我总是会问的。

sentences.en: I've written it up for you.
sentences.zh: 我已经为你写好了。

sentences.en: But this is one of the advantages.
sentences.zh: 但这正是优势之一。

sentences.en: You know, you can approach people and say, do you need any help with writing up this research?
sentences.zh: 你可以主动联系别人说：“在撰写这项研究方面，你需要帮助吗？”

sentences.en: Because then you get your name on a paper, which is amazing.
sentences.zh: 因为这样你的名字就能出现在论文上，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And research is useful for the now.
sentences.zh: 研究对当下很有用。

sentences.en: But what leads us on quite nicely to the next area of conversation is it's really useful to reflect upon as well and to help us learn about what went before us and what people's previous assumptions were about mental health.
sentences.zh: 这很好地引出了下一个话题，即反思过去以及帮助我们了解前人所做的工作和人们之前对心理健康的假设，也是非常有用的。

sentences.en: And this is really a specialist area of interest for you as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是你特别感兴趣的领域。

sentences.en: Do you want to tell us a little bit about why and what I'm talking about?
sentences.zh: 你想告诉我们一点关于为什么以及我所说的是什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's a very nice lead in.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I've always been interested in the history of psychiatry.
sentences.zh: 我一直对精神病学史很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think my very first paper actually was was a history of psychiatry paper.
sentences.zh: 我想我的第一篇论文其实就是关于精神病学史的。

sentences.en: And I just always believed that it's important to have a full understanding of of what ideas about mental health problems and diagnoses are now.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为，全面了解现在关于心理健康问题和诊断的观点是很重要的。

sentences.en: We have to understand how those ideas have evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 我们必须了解这些观点是如何随时间演变的。

sentences.en: And for some disorders, it goes right back to ancient Greece and ancient Egypt and, you know, early China and India.
sentences.zh: 对于某些疾病，可以追溯到古希腊、古埃及，以及早期的中国和印度。

sentences.en: So the very, very long routes to some of the mental disorders.
sentences.zh: 所以，一些精神疾病有着非常、非常悠久的根源。

sentences.en: Others are very modern.
sentences.zh: 其他的则非常现代。

sentences.en: And unless you you have some understanding about that, it's very difficult, I think, to to to to fully grasp the importance of, you know, of diagnoses and why words are important.
sentences.zh: 我认为，除非你对此有所了解，否则很难完全掌握诊断的重要性以及为什么词汇很重要。

sentences.en: So, as I say, I've been doing interest in that all my life.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我所说，我一生都对此很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Just in the last six months, I have started a YouTube channel on the history of mental health.
sentences.zh: 就在过去六个月里，我开了一个关于心理健康史的 YouTube 频道。

sentences.en: I, if I'm honest, I probably wouldn't have done it if it hadn't been for the help of my son doing all the technical stuff.
sentences.zh: 老实说，如果不是我儿子帮我处理所有技术方面的工作，我可能不会去做。

sentences.en: But we've so far put out, I think it's nine, nine videos on a wide range of history of mental health topics.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，我们已经发布了九个关于心理健康史广泛主题的视频。

sentences.en: And they're quite unusual.
sentences.zh: 它们相当独特。

sentences.en: I think looking at other videos out there, we're definitely trying to aim for them being quite academic.
sentences.zh: 我认为看看其他的视频，我们绝对是在努力让它们变得相当学术化。

sentences.en: So there's lots of kind of references to papers and in the, you know, the kind of the about section of the videos, I do include a kind of academic reference liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以里面有很多对论文的引用，在视频的简介部分，我也确实包含了一份学术参考书目。

sentences.en: So they are they are meant to be understandable to the general public, but to be a particular interest, I think, to to people working in mental health.
sentences.zh: 所以它们旨在让普通大众能够理解，但我认为对从事心理健康工作的人来说会特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: Well, I've watched two of them so far and honestly, I find them really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到目前为止我已经看了两个，老实说，我觉得它们真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I think it's really useful to have the theory behind it, but from an expert as well, from someone that gets it in the modern context and can portray it in a really relatable way.
sentences.zh: 我认为拥有背后的理论很有用，而且是由专家，即那些在现代背景下理解它并能以一种非常易懂的方式呈现出来的人来讲解，也很有用。

sentences.en: It's really unique.
sentences.zh: 这真的很独特。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think they're quite good.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得它们相当不错。

sentences.en: And in terms of kind of viewing figures, it's it's interesting that, you know,
sentences.zh: 就观看量而言，有趣的是，你知道，

sentences.en: it's building and also just looking at some of the other videos out there on very similar ranges of topics.
sentences.zh: 它在增长，而且看看其他关于非常相似主题范围的视频，

sentences.en: Some of them, you kind of realize that this person has really just read out a Wikipedia entry, almost word for word.
sentences.zh: 你会发现其中一些人真的只是几乎逐字逐句地读了维基百科的条目。

sentences.en: And and that's OK.
sentences.zh: 这也没关系。

sentences.en: And that's often where I start.
sentences.zh: 那通常也是我开始的地方。

sentences.en: It's a topic I don't know much about.
sentences.zh: 那是一个我不怎么了解的主题。

sentences.en: That's that's usually my starting point.
sentences.zh: 那通常是我的起点。

sentences.en: But I will definitely try and add a bit more context.
sentences.zh: 但我肯定会尝试增加更多的背景信息。

sentences.en: And what I will always try and do is is is talk about how ideas have changed over time.
sentences.zh: 而且我总是会尝试谈论观点是如何随时间变化的。

sentences.en: And it's that's particularly interesting, I think, for for more recent history.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于更近期的历史来说特别有趣。

sentences.en: So I've done a couple of videos on one in particular, I think, Rosemary Kennedy, the sister of President Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一些视频，其中一个特别提到了肯尼迪总统的妹妹罗斯玛丽·肯尼迪（Rosemary Kennedy）。

sentences.en: And she had probably a kind of mild learning disability, might even not have been below the kind of diagnostic threshold if she was formally tested.
sentences.zh: 她可能有一种轻微的学习障碍，如果进行正式测试，甚至可能达不到诊断阈值。

sentences.en: But at the time, there was huge stigma associated with that and some terrible old fashioned phrases that we, you know, it's really hard to speak them out loud nowadays.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这与巨大的耻辱感联系在一起，还有一些可怕的、老式的短语，你知道，现在真的很难大声说出来。

sentences.en: Feeble mindedness, morons, all this kind of terminology was was in the medical and psychological literature.
sentences.zh: “弱智”、“白痴”，所有这些术语都出现在医学和心理学文献中。

sentences.en: There were people writing papers about this and suggesting that they should be compulsorily sterilized.
sentences.zh: 当时有人写论文讨论这个问题，并建议应该对他们进行强制绝育。

sentences.en: And in the US, there was 60,000 people were were were sterilized because they were thought to be unfit for for breeding.
sentences.zh: 在美国，有 6 万人因为被认为不适合繁衍后代而被绝育。

sentences.en: And obviously, that went to its furthest extreme in Germany, where people with mental illness, mental learning disability were killed, were murdered.
sentences.zh: 显然，这种情况在德国达到了极端，患有精神疾病、精神学习障碍的人被杀害了，被谋杀了。

sentences.en: Thousands of them, 300,000.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人，30 万人。

sentences.en: So it's important to know.
sentences.zh: 所以了解这些很重要。

sentences.en: So this is that's just about within living memory.
sentences.zh: 这几乎还在人们的记忆之中。

sentences.en: 1930s, obviously, the war, the war period that there are fewer and fewer people around that actually remember that.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 30 年代，显然是战争时期，现在记得那段历史的人越来越少了。

sentences.en: But the kind of folk memory, if you like, of ideas and stigma and lives on.
sentences.zh: 但那种关于观点和耻辱感的民间记忆，如果可以这么说的话，依然存在。

sentences.en: And, you know, even within my career, I can see changes in the way mentally ill people have been regarded, the way psychiatry is, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，即使在我的职业生涯中，我也能看到人们对待精神病患者的方式，以及精神病学被医学界其他成员看待的方式发生了变化，你知道，

sentences.en: viewed by other members of the medical profession.
sentences.zh: 被医学界其他成员看待的方式。

sentences.en: And if I'm honest, you know, I probably would have shared some of those ideas at medical schools.
sentences.zh: 老实说，你知道，我在医学院时可能也会认同其中的一些观点。

sentences.en: Like, who wants to be a psychiatrist?
sentences.zh: 比如，谁想当精神科医生？

sentences.en: You know, that's that's terrible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, you never do anything very well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你永远做不好任何事情。

sentences.en: You never cure anyone.
sentences.zh: 你永远治不好任何人。

sentences.en: Would have been the kind of rhetoric back in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是 20 世纪 80 年代的论调。

sentences.en: And it's been, you know, over the last 30, 40 years, there has been a gradual move, a gradual acceptance that the mental illness isn't something to be ashamed of.
sentences.zh: 在过去的 30、40 年里，人们逐渐达成了一种共识，即精神疾病并不是什么丢人的事情。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, particularly in maybe in the last 10 years, we're gradually moving towards this greater acceptance.
sentences.zh: 我认为，特别是在过去 10 年里，我们正在逐渐走向这种更大的接纳。

sentences.en: But there's still a long way to go.
sentences.zh: 但还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: So there's still a lot of those ideas that were still there, you know, in the 30s, 40s, 50s.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些在 30、40、50 年代就存在的观点依然存在。

sentences.en: They're still there.
sentences.zh: 它们依然在那里。

sentences.en: They still affect people's thinking.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然影响着人们的思维。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: And I love the breadth and the depth of your experience, which I think is what your competition did not have.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你经验的广度和深度，我认为这就是你的竞争对手所不具备的。

sentences.en: Because, you know, you've earned your stripes.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，你已经赢得了你的荣誉。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And there's something to be said about aspiring psychologists learning that breadth and that depth as well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 有抱负的心理学家学习这种广度和深度也是有意义的，不是吗？

sentences.en: And learning about the importance of the theory.
sentences.zh: 并且学习理论的重要性。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, one of the things that a lot of assistant psychologists talk about is diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，很多助理心理学家谈论的一件事就是诊断。

sentences.en: And obviously, that's not necessarily a word that is the right word for psychology, but it is the way doctors work and have done for probably 2,000 years.
sentences.zh: 显然，这不一定是心理学的正确词汇，但这是医生工作的方式，而且已经持续了大约 2000 年。

sentences.en: So you've got to at least understand what a diagnosis is.
sentences.zh: 所以你至少得明白什么是诊断。

sentences.en: And sometimes I get asked questions like, what is the official diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 有时我会遇到这样的问题：“官方诊断是什么？”

sentences.en: And that one always prompts a little bit of discussion from me as I say, well, you know, a diagnosis is just an opinion.
sentences.zh: 这个问题总是会引发我的一点讨论，我会说，嗯，你知道，诊断只是一种观点。

sentences.en: And even if we say, well, they fit the criteria of DSM or ICD-10, those are just our current ideas on what the criteria should be.
sentences.zh: 即使我们说，嗯，他们符合 DSM 或 ICD-10 的标准，那也只是我们目前对标准应该是什么的看法。

sentences.en: And those have changed over time.
sentences.zh: 这些标准随着时间的推移已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: They've changed, you know, over the last 50 years and certainly over a longer period of history.
sentences.zh: 它们在过去 50 年里发生了变化，在更长的历史时期内肯定也发生了变化。

sentences.en: So a formulation actually is a more valid, individualized way of thinking about a person.
sentences.zh: 所以，构思（Formulation）实际上是一种更有效、更个性化的思考人的方式。

sentences.en: But everyone's always interested in diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 但每个人总是对诊断感兴趣。

sentences.en: So you have to fit your, or be willing to at least accommodate a diagnosis in formulations.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须适应，或者至少愿意在构思中容纳一个诊断。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, diagnosis isn't really useful because it, you know, like you said,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，诊断并不是真的很有用，因为它，你知道，就像你说的，

sentences.en: it gives us an understanding of how best to understand someone's difficulties and what might be a robust evidence-based treatment plan.
sentences.zh: 它让我们了解如何最好地理解某人的困难，以及什么是稳健的、基于证据的治疗计划。

sentences.en: But it doesn't define somebody.
sentences.zh: 但它并不能定义一个人。

sentences.en: No, and that's the big downside, obviously, of diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 不，这显然是诊断的一大缺点。

sentences.en: And it puts people into boxes and we're dealing with individuals.
sentences.zh: 它把人框住了，而我们面对的是个体。

sentences.en: And so whilst I would always have a diagnosis for a patient, you know, I also make sure that I have a lot of information on their early development, their pre-mortive personality.
sentences.zh: 所以虽然我总是会给病人一个诊断，你知道，我也确保我有关于他们早期发展、病前人格的大量信息。

sentences.en: So that, you know, you're saying, well, this is the diagnosis, but then this is the individual with this diagnosis and how it has affected them.
sentences.zh: 这样，你知道，你是在说，嗯，这是诊断，但这是带有这种诊断的个体，以及它如何影响了他们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's really useful to discuss with people as well what their diagnosis means and how they feel about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为与人们讨论他们的诊断意味着什么以及他们对此有何感受也非常有用。

sentences.en: So I work a lot with developmental trauma, I should say people who have had developmental trauma experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常与发展性创伤患者一起工作，我应该说那些有发展性创伤经历的人。

sentences.en: And a lot of them are diagnosed with borderline personality disorder or emotionally unstable personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人被诊断为边缘性人格障碍或情绪不稳定人格障碍。

sentences.en: And they really aren't OK with that because they've already been through awful, awful things, you know, pretty much from the point that they were conceived.
sentences.zh: 他们真的无法接受这一点，因为他们已经经历了可怕、可怕的事情，你知道，几乎从他们受孕的那一刻起。

sentences.en: So then to be labelled with EUPD feels like a real kick in the guts.
sentences.zh: 所以被贴上 EUPD 的标签感觉就像是在心口上狠狠踢了一脚。

sentences.en: And so it's a useful conversation to have.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有用的谈话。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，是的。

sentences.en: So I always discuss diagnosis with patients, whether they remember it, whether they want to remember it is another thing entirely.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是与病人讨论诊断，至于他们是否记得，是否想记得，那是另一回事了。

sentences.en: But for something as incendiary as EUPD is such an important diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 但对于像 EUPD 这样具有煽动性的诊断来说，这是一个非常重要的诊断。

sentences.en: But also, you know, helping patients understand that, you know, what that actually says to other people who will be reading that diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 但同时，你知道，帮助病人理解，你知道，这实际上对其他阅读该诊断的人意味着什么。

sentences.en: And sadly, it's, you know, it's not going to, you know, people are going to think, oh, right, difficult patient.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，它，你知道，它不会，你知道，人们会想，哦，对了，难缠的病人。

sentences.en: And they and I think it's useful for patients to know that that diagnoses are going to evoke emotional responses in other health care professionals.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为让病人知道诊断会引起其他医疗专业人员的情绪反应是有用的。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 肯定的。

sentences.en: I have loved speaking with you today and I honestly feel like I could speak to you all day.
sentences.zh: 今天和你谈话我非常愉快，老实说我觉得我可以和你谈上一整天。

sentences.en: But we tried to keep these episodes at about 30 minutes.
sentences.zh: 但我们尽量把这些剧集控制在 30 分钟左右。

sentences.en: So we're going to need to draw it to a close.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要结束了。

sentences.en: Have you got any final points or kind of questions or observations that you want to make?
sentences.zh: 你还有什么最后的观点，或者想提出的问题或观察吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, just really, you know, work hard at becoming part of the team, as I say, make the coffee, go and get the patients.
sentences.zh: 是的，没有了，真的，你知道，努力成为团队的一部分，正如我所说，去泡咖啡，去接病人。

sentences.en: But you will also sometimes make the coffee.
sentences.zh: 但有时你也得去煮咖啡。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: No, definitely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不行。

sentences.en: So, you know, if there's any psychiatrist listening to this, then do not expect people to make coffee for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果有什么精神科医生在听这段话，千万别指望别人为你煮咖啡。

sentences.en: Be willing to go and make it.
sentences.zh: 要乐于自己去煮。

sentences.en: So it's it's although usually that the psychiatrist is the the unelected leader of the team, there's no real reason for that.
sentences.zh: 虽然精神科医生通常是团队中非民选的领导者，但这并没有什么真正的理由。

sentences.en: There's no management responsibility that says, oh, the doctor has to be in charge.
sentences.zh: 没有任何管理职责规定医生必须负责。

sentences.en: But that's just the way most teams work, not every team, but the way most teams work and just being aware of that and working with it.
sentences.zh: 但这只是大多数团队的工作方式，并非所有团队都这样，但了解这一点并顺应它很重要。

sentences.en: And with the being aware of the kind of the history of how psychiatry, psychology and other professions have developed and all work together.
sentences.zh: 同时也要了解精神病学、心理学和其他专业是如何发展并共同协作的历史。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: It's been such an interesting episode and been a pleasure to speak to you.
sentences.zh: 这一集非常有趣，能与你交谈真是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: How can people get get connected with you?
sentences.zh: 人们该如何与你取得联系呢？

sentences.en: Where where are you at with your YouTube channel?
sentences.zh: 你的 YouTube 频道进展如何？

sentences.en: YouTube search putting Professor Graham Yorston or history of mental health that will lead to my videos.
sentences.zh: 在 YouTube 上搜索“Professor Graham Yorston”或“history of mental health”，就能找到我的视频。

sentences.en: And that's probably the easiest way to get hold of me.
sentences.zh: 那可能是找到我最简单的方法。

sentences.en: I think my son's even opened a tick tock one for me, but I don't really know what's on that yet.
sentences.zh: 我想我儿子甚至帮我开了一个 TikTok 账号，但我还不知道上面有什么内容。

sentences.en: I don't really understand tick tock, but I'm not doing any dancing.
sentences.zh: 我不太懂 TikTok，但我可不会在上面跳舞。

sentences.en: It's safe with that one.
sentences.zh: 这点大可放心。

sentences.en: So that's probably the easiest place to see me.
sentences.zh: 所以那可能是找到我最简单的地方。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Let's have a practice.
sentences.zh: 我们来练习一下。

sentences.en: What should people do when they get to your channel?
sentences.zh: 人们进入你的频道后应该做什么？

sentences.en: Oh, yes, they should.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，他们应该这样做。

sentences.en: Now, what is it called again?
sentences.zh: 现在，它叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Subscribe.
sentences.zh: 订阅。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So subscribe and like and comment.
sentences.zh: 所以，订阅、点赞并评论。

sentences.en: So comments is important.
sentences.zh: 评论很重要。

sentences.en: And one of the things you do have to be aware of, though, is you have to develop a thick skin.
sentences.zh: 不过有一点你需要注意，那就是你得练就厚脸皮。

sentences.en: So there's overwhelmingly positive comments so far.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，评论绝大多数都是积极的。

sentences.en: But by gun, there's a few absolutely horrible ones.
sentences.zh: 但天哪，确实有几条极其恶毒的评论。

sentences.en: So you have to learn to kind of not focus on those, which is, you know, it's important in life to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须学会不要关注那些评论，你知道，在生活中能做到这一点很重要。

sentences.en: So like, subscribe and click on the notification so that when the new ones come out, it goes.
sentences.zh: 所以，点赞、订阅并点击通知，这样当新视频发布时，它就会提醒你。

sentences.en: You somehow know about it miraculously by the wonder of technology.
sentences.zh: 通过科技的神奇力量，你奇迹般地就能知道它发布了。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Honestly, do it.
sentences.zh: 说真的，去做吧。

sentences.en: Do it.
sentences.zh: 去做吧。

sentences.en: And do it for this channel as well, because this one's good, too.
sentences.zh: 也为这个频道这样做，因为这个频道也很棒。

sentences.en: It's been an absolute pleasure to reconnect with you.
sentences.zh: 能与你重新联系真是太高兴了。

sentences.en: I'm wishing you all the best with your YouTube channel and beyond and book writing and all of those good things are going to be coming imminently.
sentences.zh: 祝你的 YouTube 频道、写作以及即将到来的所有好事一切顺利。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你参加我的节目。

sentences.en: And thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Hello, my name is Veronica Kasova.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫 Veronica Kasova。

sentences.en: I live in Edinburgh and I just graduated with a master's in psychology of mental health.
sentences.zh: 我住在爱丁堡，刚获得了心理健康心理学硕士学位。

sentences.en: Marian recommended me the Clinical Psychologist Collective when I was networking on LinkedIn and I must say I love it.
sentences.zh: 当我在 LinkedIn 上建立人脉时，Marian 向我推荐了《临床心理学家集体》，我必须说我爱死它了。

sentences.en: It is one of a kind.
sentences.zh: 它是独一无二的。

sentences.en: It's like a window into the lives of people on the path of becoming a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 它就像一扇窗，让我们窥见那些走在成为心理学家道路上的人们的生活。

sentences.en: The stories are unique, honest and filled with a kind of intangible wisdom only personal storytelling can uncover.
sentences.zh: 这些故事独特、真诚，充满了只有个人叙述才能揭示的那种无形的智慧。

sentences.en: A common thread in the stories I valued most was to be compassionate not only with others, but with myself, too.
sentences.zh: 我在这些故事中发现的一个共同点是，不仅要对他人的富有同情心，也要对自己富有同情心。

sentences.en: Also, not fixating on becoming a psychologist, but enjoying life, grow and the final results will come as a byproduct.
sentences.zh: 此外，不要执着于成为心理学家，而是要享受生活、成长，最终的结果会作为副产品自然到来。

sentences.en: Marian, thank you for taking the time to collate all the stories.
sentences.zh: Marian，谢谢你花时间整理了所有这些故事。

sentences.en: The book is a true gem and I think every aspiring psychologist should have a copy on their shelf.
sentences.zh: 这本书是一块真正的瑰宝，我认为每一位有抱负的心理学家都应该在书架上放一本。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: I really love to connect with you over on socials.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢在社交媒体上与你们交流。

sentences.en: LinkedIn is Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: LinkedIn 是 Dr. Marianne Trent。

sentences.en: YouTube is Good Thinking Psychological Services.
sentences.zh: YouTube 是 Good Thinking Psychological Services。

sentences.en: Facebook is also Good Thinking Psychological Services.
sentences.zh: Facebook 也是 Good Thinking Psychological Services。

sentences.en: Twitter is Good Thinking PS1.
sentences.zh: Twitter 是 Good Thinking PS1。

sentences.en: Instagram is Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: Instagram 是 Dr. Marianne Trent。

sentences.en: If TikTok is your jam, I'm also on there, too, at Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢玩 TikTok，我也在那里，账号是 Dr. Marianne Trent。

sentences.en: Being well supported during psychology application season is so important.
sentences.zh: 在心理学申请季得到良好的支持非常重要。

sentences.en: We have got one final date planned for a compassionate Q&A, which is going to be taking place on the 9th of May, Monday, the 9th of May, at 7.30pm UK time.
sentences.zh: 我们计划了最后一场同情心问答活动，时间定在 5 月 9 日，星期一，英国时间晚上 7 点 30 分。

sentences.en: And that is free to attend.
sentences.zh: 参加是免费的。

sentences.en: If you would like to watch any of the replays from the three previous episodes, then you can do so by going along to Good Thinking Psychological Services on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果你想观看前三期的回放，可以前往 YouTube 上的 Good Thinking Psychological Services。

sentences.en: And then if you click the playlist, compassionate Q&A, you'll be able to find the three previous episodes there.
sentences.zh: 点击播放列表“Compassionate Q&A”，你就能找到前三期的内容。

sentences.en: Hope you will find it useful and, as ever, would love any feedback you've got on any of our free resources.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得有用，一如既往，欢迎对我们的任何免费资源提出反馈。

sentences.en: If you are finding this podcast helpful, please do talk about it on social media.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这个播客有帮助，请在社交媒体上分享它。

sentences.en: Tag me in, tag your friends, do all of those good things.
sentences.zh: 艾特我，艾特你的朋友，做所有这些好事吧。

sentences.en: And I will look forward to catching up with you on our next episode, which will be along on Mondays at 6am UK time.
sentences.zh: 我期待在下一期节目中与你相见，节目将于每周一英国时间早上 6 点发布。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist, then let this be your guide.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名心理学家，那就让它成为你的指南吧。

sentences.en: With this podcast at your side, you'll be on your way to being qualified.
sentences.zh: 有这个播客在身边，你离获得资格就不远了。

sentences.en: It's the Aspiring Psychologist podcast with Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 这就是由 Marianne Trent 博士主持的《有抱负的心理学家》播客。

sentences.en: I'm Jo, and I work as an assistant practitioner in a CAM service in Lancashire.
sentences.zh: 我是 Jo，我在兰开夏郡的 CAM 服务中心担任助理从业者。

sentences.en: I bought and read Marianne's book, The Clinical Psychologist Collective, to accompany me while completing the clinical psychology training application.
sentences.zh: 我购买并阅读了 Marianne 的书《临床心理学家集体》，以陪伴我完成临床心理学培训申请。

sentences.en: It proved to be really good company.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，它确实是一个很好的伙伴。

sentences.en: I found it sparked ideas of how to build experience and skills, but more than that, it offered the chance to get lost in people's stories.
sentences.zh: 我发现它激发了我关于如何积累经验和技能的想法，但更重要的是，它让我有机会沉浸在人们的故事中。

sentences.en: It provided a timely reminder not to get so caught up in an end goal and to value and enjoy each job we fulfil along the way.
sentences.zh: 它及时提醒我们，不要太执着于最终目标，要珍惜并享受我们一路走来所履行的每一份工作。

sentences.en: Because the work we do now is important and matters to those we sit alongside, as well as ourselves.
sentences.zh: 因为我们现在所做的工作很重要，对我们身边的人以及我们自己都有意义。

sentences.en: It also gave the reassurance that there are eclectic routes into clinical psychology,
sentences.zh: 它还让我确信，进入临床心理学领域有多种多样的途径，

sentences.en: which is important for me as someone who's had a meandering journey and not a typical route to the profession.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很重要，因为我的职业道路比较曲折，并非典型的专业路线。

sentences.en: I wholeheartedly recommend the book for both personal and professional reasons.
sentences.zh: 我衷心推荐这本书，无论是出于个人还是职业原因。

sentences.en: Be prepared to put evening tasks on hold for a while though, because once you've started reading, it's tough to put it down.
sentences.zh: 不过要做好准备，暂时放下晚上的任务，因为一旦开始阅读，就很难停下来。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚取除了出卖时间换取金钱之外的收入，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One to Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: Sophie Foote 的“One to Many”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于 2022 年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得 Sophie 的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四次小组大师班、大师课、个性化指导、一份 Fortnum and Mason 的礼物，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。
